extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, appellants/respondents, patent attorneys and agents practicing before the Board (Part 41 contested cases/inter partes appeals)
extracted.subtask_short: Board appeal and contested case rules
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and explanation of Part 41 rules governing appeals, inter partes proceedings, and contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, including procedural, formatting, and evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board remand/reversal/affirmance and appellant rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may reverse the rejection (with or without remand to the examiner for further action), remand the appeal to the examiner for further consideration, or affirm the rejection. A final decision on appeal can only be reached when the record is susceptible to meaningful review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants under § 41.50(a)(2) may respond to any supplemental examiner’s answer by (1) requesting prosecution be reopened before the examiner by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits (§§ 1.130, 1.131 or 1.132) or other evidence; or (2) requesting the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief as provided in § 41.41. Many remands result from unclear records (e.g., amendments/additional evidence filed during appeal not clearly considered or merely 'entered' without comment). Limits on post-notice-of-appeal amendments/evidence (see § 41.33) are expected to minimize such occurrences. Upon remand the examiner may determine claims patentable and pass the case to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause for new argument in rehearing (§ 41.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In a request for rehearing the appellant may only rely on evidence previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except as amended to permit new argument upon showing good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 41.52(a) amended to permit the appellant, upon a showing of good cause, to rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court. Good cause examples include new law or facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief due date timing in inter partes appeals (§ 41.66(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant's brief is due within two months from the latest filed notice of appeal or cross appeal or within two months from the expiration of the time for filing such notice of appeal or cross appeal, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule amended to resolve ambiguity about whether the brief due date depends on another party filing a late notice of appeal; provides clarity about timing in multi-party situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on addressing other requesters' briefs (§ 41.68(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester's respondent brief may not address any brief of any other requester; however a requester may refer to arguments made in its own previously filed brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'other' was inserted to prevent multiple requesters from addressing each other's briefs which would make the proceeding unmanageable; no prohibition on referring to one's own earlier brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer requirements and reopening prosecution (§ 41.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: § 41.69 generally incorporates requirements of former § 1.969 (2003) relating to the examiner's Answer and does not change current practice in paragraphs (b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comment urging elimination of the requirement to reopen prosecution if the examiner is persuaded by a brief was not adopted; the comment suggesting additional structuring of new grounds in the Answer was not adopted here but forwarded for further consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart D contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D is designed to address all contested proceedings before the Board, including title proceedings under 42 U.S.C. 2182(4) and 2457(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title proceedings are a small percentage of contested cases; special rules for title cases would likely be placed in a new subpart if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of contested case when examination complete (§ 41.102(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 41.102(a) was amended to include language clarifying that contested cases may involve interfering subject matter which is patentable to the applicant subject to a judgment in an interference; the provision is generalized because subpart D is not limited to interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that patentability might not be an issue in some contested proceedings (e.g., title proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action in involved cases and notice (§ 41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.103 suspends action in any case involved in a contested case before the Board except as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judgment in the involved case will constitute adequate notice that the suspension is lifted. Suspension applies only to involved files, not to ancillary files (e.g., benefit files), which remain subject to timely response to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver/suspension of rules in subpart D and limits (§ 41.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative patent judge may waive or suspend a rule in subpart D subject to such conditions as the judge may impose; § 41.104(b) provides flexibility but does not authorize arbitrariness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abuse of waiver can be corrected (see § 41.125(c)(5)); the rule reflects existing Standing Order practice; balance struck between overly constrictive rules and providing guidance; similar flexibility for setting times in § 41.104(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size uniformity requirement (§ 41.106(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers from a party must be the same size absent some compelling reason for a larger paper size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Larger' means larger in any dimension that prevents reproduction without loss of detail. Smaller exhibits can usually be reproduced on standard paper; some large exhibits cannot be reduced without loss of detail, so flexibility is provided to use larger paper when truly necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-spacing exceptions (§ 41.106(a)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are required to be double-spaced except for headings, signature blocks and certificates of service; rule modified to include tables of contents, tables of authorities, and indices as exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting exceptions specifically listed to account for practical document elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page/word limits and electronic filing incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for page limits or word counts (e.g., like FRAP 32(a)(7)) were outside the scope of the present proposal but may be addressed in a pilot program or future rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing pilot programs might permit word counts as an incentive to file text-searchable papers; not adopted in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities: distinctive cover sheet and two-hole punch requirement (§ 41.106(b)(1)(ii) & (b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for distinctive cover sheets and two-hole punched paper were introduced to facilitate Board paper handling and mirror practices of courts reviewing Board decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formalities improve handling; they do not apply to interferences in the electronic filing pilot program and likely would not apply in a permanent electronic filing system; participation in pilot program permits avoiding these formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on incorporation by reference and combined papers (§ 41.106(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference from other papers and combining papers is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation and combined papers may reduce apparent length but often obscure argument flow and produce disjointed presentations lacking sufficient explanation; frustrating and confusing the decision-maker is unwise and the rule prohibits the practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief process for formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Relief from formal requirements is obtained by miscellaneous motion (§ 41.121(a)(3)); waiver of a rule in subpart D can be granted on a motion (§ 41.104(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the formalities are in a Standing Order or in a rule, the remedy for relief is a miscellaneous motion; placing the requirements in the rule reflects their near-universal present use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra copy requirement and electronic filing waiver (§ 41.106(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An extra copy is required under § 41.106(c); electronic filing is a pilot program administered under an additional order that waives the extra copy requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is expected to eliminate many formalities associated with paper filing; permanent rules for electronic filings may be proposed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand filing and equivalents (Express Mail) (§ 41.106(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 41.106(d) amended to list hand filing expressly along with electronic filing as a filing mode the Board may authorize by order; hand filing with Office mail room is not equivalent to hand filing with the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express Mail accepted as equivalent to hand filing with the Office if properly addressed; overnight delivery and other hand delivery forms treated by order. Board cautious about codifying hand filing practices due to facility access/security concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service modes and promptness alternatives (§ 41.106(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Overnight delivery is not the only alternative to EXPRESS MAIL; other prompt delivery forms (including facsimile or electronic service with Board authorization) may be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule provides latitude in meeting service requirements while still requiring promptness; modes that take much more than a day may be limited by order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of service for response period calculation (§ 41.106(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that the date to be excluded from calculating response periods is the date of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule amended to be consistent with § 41.123 and § 41.155.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service exhibit naming (§ 41.106(f)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of service must name exhibits; paragraph reordered and revised to say 'for exhibits filed as a group, the name and number of each exhibit served.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses confusion about 'each' by clarifying the requirement as to exhibits filed as a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of counsel includes patent agents (§ 41.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 41.108 uses 'counsel' consistent with § 41.5, intended to include registered patent practitioners and any person recognized to act pro hac vice (including registered patent agents who are not attorneys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that 'counsel' is inclusive of non-attorney registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to § 1.131 / § 41.202(d) declarations and withholding (§ 41.109(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of withholding access to certain declarations in involved applications was not retained; papers will be available in published applications via image file wrapper; an applicant may move (§ 41.121(a)(3)) to have a § 41.202 showing withheld if undue prejudice can be shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The image file wrapper reduces copying mistakes; withholding requests are to be decided case-by-case and the Board may advise the Office of Public Records to remove the showing from the file after printing if withholding is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting certified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in § 41.109(a) prevents requesting a certified copy of Office records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation of Office of Public Records is outside this rulemaking; image file wrapper should reduce copying mistakes that previously led to missing pages in uncertified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean copy requirement for involved claims (§ 41.110(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must file a clean copy of its involved claims; requirement strikes balance between clarity and cost and does not require clean copies of uninvolved claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clean copy of any claim to be added should be included with any motion to add the claim (§ 41.110(c)); parties may voluntarily file clean copies of uninvolved claims if easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim annotation requirement and estoppel consequences (§ 41.110)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are required to provide annotated claims; claim annotation is vital to efficient contested-case administration to show how the party intends its claim to be read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim annotation must be complete and accurate; it provides a starting point for opposing parties and the Board. Parties may point out additional support consistent with their annotation. Corrections can be sought via miscellaneous motion (§ 41.121(a)(3)), and prejudice to the opposing party is an important consideration in granting relief. Attempting to avoid prosecution estoppel is not a valid reason to evade clear claim meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single annotation per claim rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not require more than one annotation for each claim; no additional annotations are required unless a claim is added or amended (§ 41.110(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor grammatical amendments might not require a new annotation; the annotation requirement can be waived at a conference call discussing the motion in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for added claims (clean copy, claim chart, annotated copy) (§ 41.110(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended § 41.110(c) requires a clean copy, a claim chart showing written description, and an annotated copy (when applicable) of any added claim, including added claims in a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'reissue' was deleted where inapplicable; any added claim is to be treated uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of basis for relief (§ 41.120(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 41.120 authorizes the Board to require a notice outlining how a party intends to litigate a contested case (a 'notice of bases for relief'), but the content will vary with case type and greater detail in the rule is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice is not automatically required except for priority statements under § 41.204(a); when the Board requires such notice it will specify what must be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding nature of notices and potential admissions (§ 41.120(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party filing a notice of basis for relief may be restricted to filing only motions consistent with that notice; statements in such notices could be treated as admissions and interpreted against the filing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to preliminary statements practice (§ 1.629), doubts as to definiteness or sufficiency are resolved against the filing party. § 41.120(b) places parties on explicit notice that their statements might be used as admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for correcting notice of basis for relief (§ 41.120(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of a notice of basis for relief is subject to a strict 'interests-of-justice' standard (comparable to preliminary-statement correction practice), particularly where the party was on notice it would be strictly bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule does not prevent the Board from requiring other notices that are easier to correct in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of preliminary and priority motions (§ 41.123 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary motions (threshold issues, count scope, and benefit) will generally precede any priority motion since they affect the scope and complexity of any priority case to be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main effect of the rule is to have the priority case presented as a motion whenever it is filed; the Board can advance priority issues in exceptional cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to address patentability issues in interferences (§ 41.121(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not limit the Board's authority to address patentability questions so long as they relate to a change in the scope of the interference or to a change in the accorded benefit, or are otherwise likely to lead to judgment in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patentability issue should be reached in the interest of justice but is outside § 41.121, a party may seek relief under § 41.104 via a miscellaneous motion (§ 41.121(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims and consequences (§ 41.121(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation of a claim was removed as an express option to avoid casual requests, though cancellation and disclaiming remain options under 'otherwise cure a defect'. Cancellation can have consequences, including judgment against the canceling party (§ 41.127(b)(2)) and estoppel (§ 41.127(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation is not cost-free and may be treated as a concession; the rule amended to avoid casual cancellation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standards for motions (default vs exceptions) (§ 41.121(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all issues decided by motion are subject to the preponderance of the evidence standard; some (e.g., a junior party proving priority where its application filed after a patentee's patent) require clear and convincing evidence (see § 41.207(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifying preponderance as the default would require listing every exception and likely cause confusion; existing exceptions remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive burden for motions and content requirements (§ 41.121(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: § 41.121(c) contains general requirements for the contents of motions; movants must carry the substantive burden of proof regardless of rule-level detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former § 1.637 requirements were sometimes over- or under-inclusive; compliance with a procedural checklist does not substitute for proving the case on the merits. The Board may develop practice notes as experience grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts single-sentence requirement (§ 41.121(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Material facts should be stated in a manner permitting the opposing party to admit or deny the fact readily; a single-sentence requirement for material facts is added at § 41.121(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-sentence or compound statements burden opposing parties in parsing admissions/denials; the rule was amended to require clearer, single-sentence material facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of patentability when adding claims limited to written description (§ 41.121(c)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to 'prove patentability' when adding a claim has generally been limited to showing compliance with the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. 112(1), except where the party reasonably has actual notice that other patentability problems exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual notice is typically provided by a prior rejection in prosecution history or by a substantive motion by the opposing party; there is no unlimited obligation to address every conceivable rejection based solely on prosecution history.
